cards.direct.desc: Ignore suits. Reshuffle and draw A–8, A–8, A–8, then A–4 for each full word. Finish with the shorter rank sequence shown for the checksum-valid final word.
cards.help.hashed: Each valid card updates a deterministic test seed. For real security, {deal}. SHA-256 hashes the ASCII transcript (AS 2C TD).

cards.help.direct: For each of the first {partialWords} words, shuffle and draw from A–8 three times, then A–4 once. Each four-character group selects one word; spaces separate the groups. The shorter final group supplies the remaining entropy bits, and EntropyLab calculates the BIP39 checksum bits.

msig.intro: Combine extended public keys into a multisignature wallet. Paste each key origin and extended public key as exported by its signer: [fingerprint/48h/0h/0h/2h]xpub…. A descriptor holding one co-signer key works too; split a full multisig descriptor into one key per field. A trailing branch step such as /0/* is accepted and ignored — the receive/change branches and address indexes are derived for you. A longer trailing path such as /0/20 or /0/0/20/* is honored as descriptor key derivation in full: the co-signer's public keys derive through it, and the exported descriptor carries it before the branch step. Private keys are not needed. The derived addresses can receive bitcoin, and spending requires the configured number of signatures.

psbt.intro: Inspecting a PSBT v0 does not require a private key. EntropyLab can show outputs, PSBT-provided input amounts and fees, signatures, and repeated ECDSA nonce values. Optional Jade anti-exfil transcripts (host nonce ρ and signer opening R) are checked without a key. Loading a matching key additionally checks whether supported signatures match plain RFC 6979 or Bitcoin Core-style low-r grinding; a mismatch alone is not evidence of a compromised signer.

note.brainTrimmed: Brain wallet recovery: SHA-256 used the passphrase after trimming leading and trailing whitespace.

note.wifCompressed: Decoded a compressed WIF private key (starts with K or L on mainnet).
note.wifUncompressed: Decoded an uncompressed WIF private key (starts with 5 on mainnet).

note.brainLabEmpty: SHA-256 hex appears here. 24 words appear only after {derive}.
note.brainLabSha: SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 text is 32 bytes of BIP39 entropy (256 bits → 24 words).
note.brainLabOnly: Lab only. Strength is the entropy of this text, not the 24-word count.
note.brainLabFast: SHA-256(text) is unsalted and fast. Anyone who can guess the text recovers the wallet.
note.brainLabNotPassphrase: This is not a BIP39 passphrase, and it is not a Bitcoin Core hdseed or address-key backup.
note.brainLabNotCore: A valid mnemonic does not mean it is the same wallet as hashing the text as a Core private key.
note.msigWatchOnly: This is watch-only. Private keys never entered this calculator.
note.msigOrigins: Each key origin lets a signer match its seed to one co-signer.
note.msigSignerSpend: A signer is only needed when you spend.
note.msigBip45: Legacy BIP45 addresses use co-signer branch 0 for this receive and change set.
note.msigBip87: Legacy P2SH uses the selected BIP87 account paths. Keep the descriptor with every seed backup.
note.msigTaproot: Taproot script-path multisig. The internal key is the BIP341 NUMS point, so spending is only possible through the {op} script path.
note.msigListedOrder: This wallet uses {op}, so the listed co-signer order is part of the script. Reordering keys changes addresses.
note.truncatedBits: Using the first {keep} mapped bits of {have}. Extra bits are not mixed in.

psbt.jadeMatch: Matches Jade anti-exfil (sign-to-contract). Host entropy mixed into the nonce. Not a leak.
psbt.jadeMismatch: Does not match this Jade anti-exfil transcript. Signature r is not R + H(R||ρ)G.
psbt.jadeAlsoNoRfc: Also does not match RFC 6979 or low-r grind.

psbt.reusedNonce: Reused nonce detected for the same public key.
psbt.reusedNonceBody: The same r value appears on different message digests. If both signatures are valid, the private key can be recovered. Do not broadcast this transaction.
psbt.possibleReuse: Possible repeated nonce for the same public key.
psbt.possibleReuseBody: The message digests could not both be reconstructed, so verify these signatures independently before treating this as a key leak.
psbt.incompleteNonceBody: Some ECDSA signatures could not be inspected, so this is not a clean verdict.
psbt.noRepeated: No repeated ECDSA nonce r values were found for the same public key in this PSBT.
psbt.oneSignature: Only one ECDSA signature with a readable r is present. Nonce reuse cannot be judged from this file alone.
psbt.noEcdsa: No ECDSA signatures with a readable r value are present, so there is no nonce to compare yet.
psbt.taprootNoteOne: This PSBT also contains {n} Taproot / Schnorr signature. It is counted but its BIP340 nonce is not analyzed in this version.
psbt.taprootNoteMany: This PSBT also contains {n} Taproot / Schnorr signatures. They are counted but their BIP340 nonces are not analyzed in this version.
psbt.rfcFootnote: RFC 6979 comparison currently covers SegWit v0 P2WPKH and P2WSH signatures using SIGHASH_ALL, including Bitcoin Core-style low-r grinding. Jade anti-exfil is secp256k1-zkp sign-to-contract and needs the USB host nonce plus signer opening; QR / sign_psbt Jade does not run it yet. BitBox anti-klepto is a different construction. Nonce reuse detection compares r values for the same secp256k1 point, including compressed and uncompressed encodings and recoverable non-strict DER. A clean verdict is not issued when a signature cannot be inspected.
psbt.rfcPlainHigh: Matches RFC 6979 (plain deterministic nonce). r is high; Bitcoin Core would grind this one.
psbt.rfcGrind: Matches RFC 6979 with Bitcoin Core-style low-r grind (retry {n}). Saves one byte. Not a leak.
psbt.rfcZeros: Matches RFC 6979 with 32 zero extra-entropy bytes (some libraries mix this in).
psbt.rfcMismatch: Does not match plain RFC 6979 or Bitcoin Core-style low-r grind. Honest signers may add other auxiliary randomness. A mismatch alone is not evidence of compromise. Reused r on two different messages is the real alarm.
psbt.problemDeclared: The PSBT requests {policy}, which does not commit to all shown outputs.
psbt.problemSuffix: This signature uses {policy}, which does not commit to all shown outputs.
psbt.problemDisagree: The PSBT-declared policy and the signature's appended sighash byte disagree.
